I have farmed this land for thirty years, and I know every corner of my 4.1 mu. My husband and I are getting older, and there are only the two of us left at home now, so we cannot manage too much land. But this 4.1 mu of wheat-maize rotation is just right for us. I have well water, which is my lifeline — when the rain does not come, I can still irrigate.

For the winter wheat, I will sow it right after National Day in early October, just like I have done every year. I will use the rotary tiller to prepare the ground first — the soil needs to be loose and fine for wheat. I will buy improved wheat seed from the village supply shop, about 30 jin per mu. I will spread compound fertilizer as basal — the kind with nitrogen, phosphate, and potassium — and then topdress with urea at green-up time. Wheat needs water at three key times: the winter irrigation to protect it from freezing, then at jointing, and once more at grain filling. I also need to spray for weeds once and for insects twice, and maybe fungicide if the weather turns damp. If all goes well, I expect about 1000 jin per mu.

For summer maize, there is no time to waste after harvesting wheat in early June. I will plant hybrid maize seed directly into the stubble without tilling — everyone here does it this way now, and it saves time and diesel. The maize grows fast in the summer heat. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting, and maybe a little extra nitrogen later if the leaves look yellow. Maize needs less irrigation than wheat — usually twice is enough, once when it is knee-high and once at flowering, as long as the summer rains are normal. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice because the corn borer is troublesome every year. With good weather, this maize should give me around 1100 jin per mu.
